nodes.description: Subretinal delivery of an adeno-associated viral vector expressing CNGB1 cDNA under a short, rod-specific promoter (required because the large CNGB1 cDNA, ~3.76-4 kb, consumes most of the AAV packaging capacity). Preclinical proof-of-concept in the Cngb1-/- mouse and a subsequent translatable construct tested in CNGB1-mutant dogs and non-human primates both showed robust, durable (at least 12-23 month) restoration of rod-mediated function and preservation of retinal structure. As of curation, this program has not yet been reported in a human clinical trial, but the combination of a wide therapeutic window (early functional loss with late structural loss) and validated large-eye preclinical efficacy makes CNGB1-RP a leading translational candidate among inherited retinal degenerations.

nodes.description: CNGB1a is required for trafficking the heteromeric rod CNG channel to the outer segment plasma membrane. In its absence, the partner CNGA1 subunit is not stably retained at the outer segment and only trace amounts remain, so the functional heterotetrameric channel fails to assemble. Structural work shows this is mediated by a specific intersubunit interaction between CNGA1 and CNGB1 that, when disrupted, exposes a trafficking-inhibitory region of CNGB1 and prevents membrane expression of the complex.

evidence.reference_title: An intersubunit interaction regulates trafficking of rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channels and is disrupted in an inherited form of blindness.
evidence.snippet: We show that the mechanism underlying this defect involves an intersubunit interaction between CNGA1 and CNGB1 that was not formed between CNGA1-RP and CNGB1 subunits. In the absence of this interaction, a short N-terminal region in CNGB1 prevented membrane expression.

evidence.reference_title: The retinitis pigmentosa mutation c.3444+1G>A in CNGB1 results in skipping of exon 32.
evidence.snippet: Here, we investigated the splicing of c.3444+1G>A by exon trapping experiments and could demonstrate that instead of the proposed truncation of the last 28 aa this mutation leads to replacement of the last 170 aa of CNGB1a by 68 unrelated amino acids.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic CNGB1 variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, and missense changes distributed across the gene's 33 exons with no known mutational hotspot) abolish or truncate the beta subunit of the rod cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. CNGB1a is the accessory subunit of the native rod channel, which is a heterotetramer of three CNGA1 subunits and one CNGB1a subunit.

nodes.description: With essentially no functional heterotetrameric CNG channel present at the outer segment, rods cannot generate a light response: the channel cannot open in response to cGMP regardless of light exposure. This produces both a functional silencing of rod phototransduction and an abnormal accumulation of cGMP within the rod outer segment, directly demonstrated by immunolabeling in CNGB1-deficient dog retina and shown to be reversible by restoring channel expression via gene therapy.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint of rod-then-cone loss: childhood-onset night blindness followed, often many decades later, by peripheral visual field constriction and eventual central vision loss. The unusually long interval between functional rod loss and structural/visual-field loss is the defining clinical feature of CNGB1-related retinopathy relative to other RP subtypes.

nodes.description: Unlike the stationary phenotype seen with some phototransduction-cascade lesions, chronic loss of CNG channel function in CNGB1-deficient rods hands off to a slowly progressive photoreceptor cell-death programme. Rods undergo apoptotic death accompanied by retinal gliosis; this is notably slower than in many other RP mouse models, producing the characteristic dissociation between early functional loss and late structural loss that defines the clinical course.

nodes.description: Cones do not express CNGB1a and are not cell-autonomously affected by the channel-trafficking defect, but they decline secondarily and later than rods once the surrounding rod population is lost, following the conserved non-cell-autonomous cone degeneration pattern of retinitis pigmentosa. This secondary, delayed cone decline underlies the retained good central vision that characterizes the disease for years after rod function is already lost.
